findings.claim: The May 2025 Software developers row reports employment 1,687,890; mean hourly USD71.20; mean annual USD148,100; median hourly USD65.38.
findings.qualification: These are reviewer-normalized facts from HTML Table 1, not workbook column names. Published May 15,2026; wages are rates, not realized annual earnings.

findings.claim: The May 2025 estimate pools six panel reference periods from November 2022 through May 2025.
findings.qualification: Four of six panels overlap adjacent annual releases, inferred from the documented rotation. Panel reference dates are not individual response dates.

findings.claim: 2019–2020 use hybrid 2010/2018 SOC; 2021 is fully 2018 SOC and introduces MB3; 2022 changes wage processing and adopts 2022 NAICS; 2025 exposes some previously top-coded percentiles.
findings.qualification: No title-only historical joins. Retain SOC and NAICS editions, geographic boundaries, suppression, uncertainty and estimation regime.

findings.claim: National/state/area history reaches 1997, but nonmetropolitan series begin May 2006; separate industry estimates also exist for 1988–1995.
findings.qualification: This is not a balanced geography/occupation panel. Earlier occupational and industry definitions differ.

findings.claim: MB3 research estimates for 2015–2020 are alternatives from shared survey evidence.
findings.qualification: Preserve the original and MB3 estimation regimes instead of silently overwriting or counting them as independent evidence.

findings.claim: BLS explicitly permits reuse of published statistical material in the public domain and requests source credit.
findings.qualification: The selected statistical table is covered; this does not waive image, emblem or third-party exceptions.

limitations: Annualized wages generally use hourly rates times2080, with occupation-specific exceptions; not annual earnings or employee income.
Survey pooling, sampling, modeling, inflation, occupation/industry recoding, geography and macroeconomic/labor-supply changes limit naive trends.
No establishment AI-adoption/outcome linkage verified. Exposure-score joins are derived analyses, not observed AI effects.
Workbook schema remains uninspected; ZIP header availability does not establish file integrity or sheet semantics.

cross_source_relationships.decision: Keep AI use and ICT training separate table/indicator identities. Correlated aggregate country-size-industry shares do not establish same firms or a causal link.

StatCan CSBC retrospective adoption, SDTIU-linked administrative productivity, Indeed advertisement text and Eurostat training use different programs/frames/denominators. Do not join on Canada/period as if employer identifiers existed.

Fresh two PDFs have different SHA256 but whitespace-normalized extracted text is identical; maintain distinct artifact hashes plus mirror/version relationship. Q28 employment effect and Q29 training/hiring are respondent attributions, not causal identification; no fifth admission.
O*NET wage display sources BLS OEWS; O*NET employment/projections display sources BLS Employment Projections. Do not double count wages or reconcile 1,717,800 vs 1,687,890 as a typo/AI effect.
OEWS MB3 research 2015–2020 and original releases are same underlying survey family, with distinct estimation regimes/revisions.
Same country-day posting series is one evidence family. Separate US contextual sample analysis is a methodological annotation, not a universal adjustment or independent set of hiring observations.

isoc_ske_ittn2 and isoc_ske_itts presentations can overlap in underlying cells; match full dimensions and publication version before merging. Specific current DESI-cell relationship not independently reverified.
Unchanged task ratings in later database releases are republications, not new fieldwork. Emerging Tasks are separate evidence type.
No particular AI Index artifact was verified to duplicate these series; do not turn shared institution/source mentions into confirmed overlap.

overlap_review.scope_note: All 15 baseline files were read in full locally after exact Git blob comparison to fresh current tree. overlap_review.url_comparison_qualification: Exact URL arrays compare the explicitly listed selected source/data URLs, not every metadata or rights URL in the final catalog. A generic CC BY license URL shared with concentration, organizational-safety, or scientific-progress catalogs is a rights-reference overlap, not shared underlying data or study.
